# Checked-in benchmark evidence. Each dated snapshot retains its original units
# and command; only its own heading defines whether it is historical or current.
# Snapshot A: perf-wave workload matrix, one iteration per workload (-count=1).
# Command (2026-08-09, working tree after lint wave + perf wave):
#   go test ./internal/convert -run '^$' -bench 'Benchmark(PDFPages|TemplatePages|WebFetchImage|ImageAssets)$' -benchmem -benchtime=1x -count=1
# Snapshot A toolchain: go1.26.4 linux/amd64 · Host: WSL2 24 CPUs · i7-13700HX
# Snapshot A raw rows below are the authoritative values for this capture.
# Main wave drivers: single cmap lookup per rune (GlyphAdvancePoints), no
# duplicate min-content re-measure, in-place inline-item compaction, ASCII
# fast paths in TextShow/html scanning, rune-union dedup in font subsetting,
# pointer-compare op sorts, zero-crossing split fast path, styleGroups hoist.
# Earlier wkhtmltopdf 0.12.6.1 process reference: 2.05s / ~114MB peak RSS / ~2.0MB PDF.
# This is process-level RSS, while Go B/op is cumulative allocation traffic;
# the values are not directly comparable.

# Snapshot B: separately recorded certified-workspace matrix sample, one
# iteration per workload (-count=1). It is not the same capture as Snapshot A.
# Command (2026-08-09; feature/optimization):
#   go test ./internal/convert -run '^$' -bench 'Benchmark(PDFPages|TemplatePages|WebFetchImage|ImageAssets)$' -benchmem -benchtime=1x -count=1
# Snapshot B summary: PDF 500: 518,117,894 ns/op / 157,636,704 B/op / 529,451 allocs/op.
# Snapshot B summary: Template 500: 552,115,316 ns/op / 162,493,632 B/op / 580,715 allocs/op.
# Snapshot B toolchain: go1.26.4 linux/amd64 · Host: WSL2 24 CPUs · i7-13700HX
# The full Snapshot B matrix is summarized in testdata/golden/benchmarks/README.md.
# Generated PDF artifacts were refreshed locally but intentionally are not
# included in the benchmark snapshot commit.

goos: linux

# Snapshot D direct CLI process rows: one freshly built pre-CR-02 binary
# run per generated report (2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 250, and 500 pages).
# Command pattern:
#   /usr/bin/time -f 'TIME elapsed_s=%e peak_rss_kib=%M' \
#     <fresh-binary> --quiet --enable-local-file-access <report-N.html> <report-N.pdf>
# Every output was verified with Ghostscript's pdfpagecount. Elapsed time is
# rounded by the centisecond timer; RSS is peak KiB. This is process evidence,
# not Go allocation evidence, and the full command/workload description is in
# testdata/golden/benchmarks/README.md.
